subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Should this broad org/team deployment umbrella remain a core OpenClaw product track, and if so which slice should be the first supported milestone?
rationale: The request would create new public config/CLI and security semantics across workspace scaffolding, deployment manifests, session or tenant RBAC, and docs, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and trust-boundary direction.

options.title: Keep umbrella and decompose
options.body: Use this issue as the broad tracker and sponsor narrower design issues for manifest/scaffold, scope/tenant RBAC, identity modes, and docs before code work.

options.title: Route most setup to external tooling
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core focused on missing extension APIs and document existing multi-gateway/plugin/front-layer patterns for org deployment.

options.title: Close in favor of narrower trackers
options.body: Declare the broad umbrella too large and track only the existing focused issues such as per-session policy, tenant RBAC, token identity, lanes, and identity modes.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and decompose
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the broad tracker and sponsor narrower design issues for manifest/scaffold, scope/tenant RBAC, identity modes, and docs before code work.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history signal across agents CLI, trust-boundary docs, and sender-policy hardening, and the choice is a core product/security direction decision.
